places.name: Rishikesh
places.summary: Yoga capital on the Ganga at the foot of the Himalaya: ashrams, the Triveni Ghat aarti, the Beatles Ashram and white-water rafting from Shivpuri.
places.seoTitle: Rishikesh Travel Guide: Yoga, Rafting & Ganga Aarti
places.seoDescription: Plan a Rishikesh trip: ashrams and yoga, the Triveni Ghat aarti, Beatles Ashram, rafting from Shivpuri (Sept–June), where to stay and how to get there.

images.alt: Ganga flowing past the temples and ghats of Rishikesh

overview.text:
Rishikesh sits where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya, with the river flowing through the town and the hills rising behind it. It is one of north India's great pilgrimage and tourist centres, and it is widely called the yoga capital of the world. Ashrams line both banks, many teaching yoga, meditation and philosophy, and Uttarakhand Tourism holds the International Yoga Festival here every March.

The town also has a famous musical past. In February 1968 the Beatles came to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram to learn transcendental meditation, and they wrote many White Album songs there. Today that ashram's forest ruins are one of the most-visited sights.

Rishikesh is also an adventure hub: white-water rafting from Shivpuri, bungee jumping, ziplines and treks. It is the gateway to the Garhwal Himalaya and the start of the Char Dham route. The city is vegetarian-only and alcohol-free.

best_time.text:
Rishikesh is pleasant to visit for most of the year. For rafting, come between September and June: the river is closed to rafting in July and August, when the monsoon swells the Ganga.

The first week of March brings the International Yoga Festival, run by Uttarakhand Tourism with Parmarth Niketan. Ashrams and yoga schools fill up then. The monsoon months are green and quiet, but expect rain, no rafting and possible landslides on the hill roads beyond town.

local_transport.text:
Rishikesh is spread along both banks of the Ganga. Taxis and shared buses link the railway station and town with Muni-ki-Reti and Swargashram. Across the river, the ashram area around Ram Jhula is mostly explored on foot.

The old Lakshman Jhula bridge is closed for safety. Its glass replacement, Bajrang Setu, was still under construction in April 2026, so cross at Ram Jhula and check locally whether Bajrang Setu has opened. For Shivpuri, Neelkanth, Narendranagar or Byasi, hire a taxi or join a rafting operator's transfer.

items.title: Rishikesh town and Triveni Ghat
items.body: The pilgrim centre, with the bathing ghat, the evening aarti and Bharat Mandir. Closest to the railway and bus stations.

items.title: Swargashram (east bank)
items.body: A cluster of ashrams offering yoga courses, including Parmarth Niketan, with the Beatles Ashram in the forest nearby. Car-light and walkable.

items.title: Muni-ki-Reti
items.body: The west bank by Ram Jhula, linked to town by taxis and buses, with ashrams and guesthouses.

items.title: Lakshman Jhula area
items.body: Upstream, around the closed old bridge and the new Bajrang Setu, with Gita Bhawan and shops. Rafting from Shivpuri ends here.

items.title: Shivpuri and beyond
items.body: 19–30 km upstream: riverside camps and rafting starts at Shivpuri and Byasi.

where_to_stay.text:
Stay in Swargashram or Muni-ki-Reti if you're here for yoga. Many ashrams in Swargashram take residents for courses, and the area is quiet and walkable.

Rishikesh town near Triveni Ghat is most convenient for the railway and buses, and for the evening aarti. For rafting, riverside camps upstream around Shivpuri and Byasi put you on the water first thing. Remember that the whole town is vegetarian and alcohol-free, and that includes hotels.

items.title: Yoga and meditation seekers
items.body: Ashram courses all year, and the International Yoga Festival in early March.

items.title: Adventure lovers
items.body: Rafting from Shivpuri (September–June), bungee and swings at Mohanchatti, ziplining and rock climbing.

items.title: Pilgrims
items.body: The Triveni Ghat aarti, Bharat Mandir and Neelkanth Mahadev. Rishikesh is also the start of the Char Dham route.

items.title: Music fans
items.body: The Beatles Ashram, where the band wrote much of the White Album in 1968.
Rishikesh is a vegetarian-only, alcohol-free city. Don't bring meat or drink into town or your hotel.
The sale of meat, fish and eggs has been banned here since 1956. The ban extends to Muni-ki-Reti, and the Supreme Court upheld the egg ban in 2004.
Dress modestly and remove shoes at temples and ghats. Join the aarti quietly.
Ashrams have their own rules on timings, silence and dress. Read them when you check in.

items.title: Getting in
items.body: Jolly Grant airport (21 km), with daily Delhi flights. Frequent trains to Rishikesh. Buses from Delhi ISBT Kashmiri Gate.

items.title: Rafting
items.body: Use certified operators. The season runs September to June, with no rafting in July and August.

items.title: Food
items.body: Vegetarian only. No alcohol is served anywhere in the city.

items.title: Crossing the river
items.body: Use Ram Jhula. The old Lakshman Jhula is closed, and you should check locally whether Bajrang Setu has opened.
Arrive at Triveni Ghat early for the evening aarti and find a spot on the steps.
Book rafting with a certified operator and choose the grade that suits you. Shivpuri to Lakshman Jhula (about 11 km) is the classic run.
Plan a March visit around the International Yoga Festival, or avoid that week if you want quiet ashrams.
Leave half a day for Neelkanth Mahadev, 28 km away through the forest.
Planning to raft in July or August, when rafting on the Ganga is suspended.
Expecting to walk across Lakshman Jhula: the old bridge is closed. Use Ram Jhula.
Packing a bottle or a meat picnic. Rishikesh is vegetarian-only and alcohol-free.
Treating the Beatles Ashram as a quick stop. It's a walk into the forest; give it two hours.

items.title: Is rafting open all year in Rishikesh?
items.body: No. The season is September to June, and rafting is suspended in July and August for the monsoon.

items.title: Is Lakshman Jhula open?
items.body: The old Lakshman Jhula is closed for safety. Its replacement, the Bajrang Setu glass bridge, was still under construction in April 2026. Use Ram Jhula and check locally.

items.title: Can I get alcohol or meat in Rishikesh?
items.body: No. Rishikesh is a vegetarian-only, alcohol-free city, and the sale of meat, fish and eggs is banned.

items.title: How do I get to Rishikesh from Delhi?
items.body: Fly to Jolly Grant (21 km away), take a train to Rishikesh station, or take a bus from Delhi's ISBT Kashmiri Gate.

items.title: When is the International Yoga Festival?
items.body: In the first week of March each year.

places.name: Triveni Ghat
places.summary: Rishikesh's main bathing ghat on the Ganga, known for its lamp-lit evening aarti.
places.seoTitle: Triveni Ghat Rishikesh: Evening Ganga Aarti
places.seoDescription: Triveni Ghat is Rishikesh's best-known bathing ghat, with a lamp-lit evening Ganga aarti. What to expect and nearby Bharat Mandir.

images.alt: Statue of Krishna's chariot beside the Ganga at Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh

overview.text:
Triveni Ghat, in the heart of Rishikesh town, is the most famous of its bathing ghats: stone steps leading down into the Ganga. Most pilgrims take a holy dip here before visiting the town's temples.

The highlight is the evening aarti. Lamps are lit across the ghat to the sound of drums and chanting, and the whole riverside flickers with light. One of Rishikesh's oldest shrines, Bharat Mandir, stands nearby, so the two make an easy late-afternoon pairing. Come early to find a place on the steps, dress modestly and leave your shoes at a stall.

items.body: Arrive before dusk to find space on the steps for the aarti.
Leave shoes at a stall and dress modestly.
Visit Bharat Mandir nearby beforehand.

images.alt: Domed stone meditation huts at the Beatles Ashram in the forest near Rishikesh

overview.text:
In February 1968 the Beatles came to Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram in Rishikesh to learn transcendental meditation. They composed nearly 48 songs here, many of which appear on the White Album. The ashram, also called Chaurasi Kutia, lies in a forest patch in the Swargashram area.

Today you can wander the ruins: domed stone meditation huts, halls and walls covered in striking murals of the band members. It's peaceful and shaded, a good contrast to the busy ghats.

items.body: In the forest of the Swargashram area, on the east bank of the Ganga.

items.title: Entry fee and hours
items.body: Charged by the forest department. Published figures vary between sources, so check at the gate.

items.title: Time needed
items.body: Allow about two hours to walk the grounds.

places.name: Swargashram
places.summary: A cluster of ashrams on the Ganga's east bank, the centre of Rishikesh's yoga courses.
places.seoDescription: Swargashram is the cluster of ashrams on Rishikesh's east bank, home to yoga and spiritual courses, Parmarth Niketan and the Beatles Ashram nearby.

images.alt: Temples and ashrams on the Ganga bank at Swargashram, Rishikesh

overview.text:
Swargashram is the name for the cluster of ashrams on the eastern bank of the Ganga. Most of them offer courses in yoga and spiritual studies and are well known among visitors. Parmarth Niketan, one of the largest ashrams, is here, and the Beatles Ashram lies in the forest just beyond.

It is linked to the west bank by Ram Jhula. Taxis and buses run between Rishikesh town and Swargashram, but the area itself is best explored on foot, along the riverside paths between ashrams, temples and cafés. Many visitors base themselves here for a week or more of classes, joining morning yoga and evening satsangs.

items.title: Yoga students
items.body: Ashram courses in yoga and spiritual studies.

items.title: Walkers
items.body: A riverside area that is best explored on foot.

places.name: Parmarth Niketan

places.seoTitle: Parmarth Niketan Rishikesh: Ashram & Yoga Festival
places.seoDescription: Parmarth Niketan, founded in 1942 on the Ganga in Swargashram, is one of Rishikesh's largest ashrams and hosts the annual International Yoga Festival.

overview.text:
Parmarth Niketan was established in 1942 by Swami Sukhdevanand Ji Maharaj on the bank of the Ganga in Swargashram. It is one of the largest and most popular ashrams in Rishikesh, a calm setting for yoga and meditation.

It is best known for the annual yoga festival it hosts. The International Yoga Festival takes place each year in the first week of March and draws yoga students from around the world, so book well ahead if you want to stay then. At other times the riverside grounds are a peaceful place for a morning class.

items.body: Book early for the first week of March, during the International Yoga Festival.
Combine with a walk to the Beatles Ashram, in the forest nearby.

places.seoDescription: Bharat Mandir near Triveni Ghat is one of Rishikesh's oldest shrines, said to have been founded by Adi Shankaracharya, with a saligram idol of Vishnu.

overview.text:
Bharat Mandir stands near Triveni Ghat and is one of the oldest shrines in Rishikesh. Tradition says the sage Adi Shankaracharya built it. The temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu, whose idol is carved from a single black stone known as a saligram.

The temple is especially lively at Basant Panchami, the spring festival. It is a short walk from the ghat, so visit it before the evening aarti. The temple is in the busy old part of town, close to the bus stand and the main bazaar, and easy to combine with a walk along the river and an evening at Triveni Ghat.

how_to_reach.text: In Rishikesh town, a short walk from Triveni Ghat. Taxis and buses reach the town centre from the railway station.

overview.text:
Shivpuri lies 19 km upstream of Rishikesh and is the main base for white-water rafting on the Ganga. The most common stretch, about 11 km, runs from Shivpuri down to Lakshman Jhula. Certified operators run trips for every grade.

The rafting season is September to June; rafting is suspended in July and August for the monsoon. Further upstream, Byasi (30 km from Rishikesh) is another rafting and water-sports hub on a scenic road. Riverside camps line this stretch of the Ganga, and many rafters spend a night here to be on the water early. Always raft with a certified operator and wear the life jacket and helmet you are given.

how_to_reach.text: Shivpuri is 19 km from Rishikesh by road. Most rafting operators include transfers, or hire a taxi.

places.seoTitle: Narendranagar near Rishikesh: Views & Old Tehri Capital
places.seoDescription: Narendranagar, the old capital of Tehri state, sits at 1,326 m just 20 km from Rishikesh, with views over the Ganga and the Doon valley.

images.alt: Lawns and gateway of the royal palace estate at Narendranagar

overview.text:
Narendranagar is a small, picturesque town in Tehri Garhwal district. It was once the capital of the princely state of Tehri. At 1,326 m and just 20 km above Rishikesh, it has a mild climate that draws visitors all year.

The town is far less visited than Rishikesh, so expect peace and quiet, and wide views over the Ganga and the Doon valley. The old royal palace estate is a reminder of its past. It makes an easy half day out of Rishikesh, especially in the monsoon when rafting is closed, and the cooler air is a welcome change from the riverside in summer.

how_to_reach.text: Narendranagar is a 20 km drive uphill from Rishikesh. Take a taxi, or a bus heading towards Tehri.

overview.text: Mohanchatti, near Rishikesh, is the place for bungee jumping, with jumps of up to 83 m. The same site offers a flying fox, giant mountain swings and paragliding. Rishikesh also has a zipline that drops to about 7 m above the river at speeds of up to 160 km/h.

places.summary: The famous old suspension bridge, now closed, and its glass replacement under construction.
places.seoTitle: Lakshman Jhula Rishikesh: Closed & Bajrang Setu
places.seoDescription: Rishikesh's old Lakshman Jhula bridge is closed for safety; the Bajrang Setu glass footbridge replacing it was under construction in April 2026.

overview.text: The old Lakshman Jhula suspension bridge, long Rishikesh's most famous landmark, was closed to traffic after it grew unsafe. Bajrang Setu, a glass footbridge at the same spot, has been under construction since 2022 and was not yet open in April 2026. Until it is, cross the river at Ram Jhula and check the bridge's status locally.

places.seoDescription: Gita Bhawan near Lakshman Jhula in Rishikesh runs a free Ayurvedic dispensary and a Gita Press branch, with scenes from the epics painted on its walls.

overview.text: Gita Bhawan, near Lakshman Jhula, runs a free Ayurvedic dispensary and a branch of the Gita Press bookshop. Its walls are painted with scenes from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, which makes it worth a short stop on a walk along the east bank.

itineraries.title: Rishikesh in 2 days: ashrams, the Beatles Ashram and a rafting run

itineraries.seoTitle: Rishikesh 2-Day Itinerary: Yoga, Beatles Ashram, Aarti & Rafting
itineraries.seoDescription: Two days in Rishikesh: a yoga class, Parmarth Niketan, the Beatles Ashram (10 am–4 pm), the Triveni Ghat aarti, and rafting the 11 km run from Shivpuri.

plan.overview: Two days covering both sides of Rishikesh. Day 1 is spiritual: a morning yoga class in Swargashram, Parmarth Niketan on the Ganga, the Beatles Ashram in the forest (open 10 am–4 pm), Ram Jhula and Bharat Mandir, and the lamp-lit aarti at Triveni Ghat at dusk. Day 2 is the river: the classic rafting run from Shivpuri, about 11 km down to Lakshman Jhula, with an easy afternoon in the cafés.

The Beatles Ashram is inside Rajaji Tiger Reserve and closes at 4 pm.
The old Lakshman Jhula is closed; cross by Ram Jhula.

Day 2 rafts the 11 km run from Shivpuri, with an optional 83 m bungee jump at Mohanchatti. Day 3 drives 28 km into the forest to the Neelkanth Mahadev temple, then climbs to Kunjapuri Devi (1,676 m), about 27.5 km from Rishikesh, for the evening view of the snow peaks.

itineraries.title: Haridwar and Rishikesh in 5 days: aarti, yoga and the Ganga
itineraries.summary: Two evening aartis on the Ganga, the Mansa Devi hilltop, yoga in Rishikesh, the Beatles Ashram, a rafting morning and a sunrise at Kunjapuri — with short transfers and no long drives.
itineraries.seoTitle: Haridwar & Rishikesh 5-Day Itinerary: Aarti, Yoga & Rafting
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic 5-day Haridwar and Rishikesh plan with aarti times, Beatles Ashram fees, rafting season and the Kunjapuri sunrise drive — short transfers throughout.

plan.overview: Haridwar and Rishikesh sit only about 25 km apart where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya, so this trip spends its time at the river rather than on the road. Start in Haridwar for the great evening aarti at Har ki Pauri, then move up to Rishikesh for yoga, the ashrams, the Beatles Ashram in the forest, a morning on the rapids, and a pre-dawn drive to the Kunjapuri hilltop.
plan.style: Spiritual and wellness, with one adventure morning
plan.start: Haridwar Junction (direct trains from Delhi) or Jolly Grant airport, Dehradun
plan.end: Jolly Grant airport (about 21 km from Rishikesh) or Haridwar station
plan.season: September–November and February–April are the best months. Rafting runs September to June and stops in July–August for the monsoon. Avoid the Kanwar fortnight in the monsoon month of Shravan if you dislike crowds.
plan.difficulty: Easy to moderate (rafting and the waterfall walk are optional)
plan.transport: Taxi or bus Haridwar → Rishikesh (25 km); walking, shared autos and taxis in Rishikesh.

days.title: Day 1 — Haridwar: Har ki Pauri aarti
days.summary: Arrive, walk the old bazaar, and take a place on the ghats for the evening aarti.

stops.note: Haridwar's oldest market — bangles, beads, sweets and Ayurvedic medicines.

stops.name: Har ki Pauri Ganga aarti
stops.note: Arrive 30–45 minutes early for a spot on the steps or the bridge opposite. The aarti starts around 5:30 pm in winter and 6:30 pm in summer.

days.travel: Haridwar station has direct trains from Delhi and other cities; Jolly Grant airport is 37 km away.
days.transport: Train or taxi; walking in the old town
days.meals: Haridwar is largely vegetarian — chaat and pakoras near the ghats.
days.logistics: Leave valuables at the hotel; the ghats get very crowded at aarti time.

days.title: Day 2 — Mansa Devi, then up to Rishikesh
days.summary: A hilltop shrine above Haridwar in the morning, the short move to Rishikesh, and the Triveni Ghat aarti at dusk.

stops.name: Mansa Devi Temple, Bilwa Parvat
stops.note: One of Haridwar's three Siddhpeeths; reach it by ropeway or the stepped path.

stops.name: Ram Jhula and Swargashram
stops.note: Cross the 1986 suspension bridge to the ashram side.

stops.name: Triveni Ghat aarti
stops.note: Rishikesh's best-known ghat; lamps, drums and chanting at dusk.

days.travel: Haridwar → Rishikesh about 25 km (about 30 minutes by taxi, 45 by bus).
days.meals: Rishikesh is vegetarian-only and alcohol-free; lunch at a riverside café on the ashram side.
days.overnight: Rishikesh (Tapovan or the Ram Jhula side)

days.title: Day 3 — Yoga, the Beatles Ashram and Parmarth Niketan
days.summary: A morning class, the forest ashram where the Beatles stayed in 1968, and an afternoon at one of the town's largest ashrams.

stops.name: Drop-in yoga class
stops.note: Many ashrams and schools take drop-ins; ask at your hotel the day before.

stops.name: Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia)
stops.note: Ruined meditation huts and murals inside Rajaji Tiger Reserve, about 1 km from Ram Jhula. Open 10 am–4 pm.

stops.name: Parmarth Niketan
stops.note: Founded in 1942 on the Ganga; the grounds and ghat are open to visitors.

days.travel: All on the Swargashram side, mostly on foot.
days.meals: Sattvic thali at an ashram canteen or a riverside café.

days.title: Day 4 — Rafting the Ganga and the Neer waterfall walk
days.summary: A morning on the rapids with a licensed operator, and an easy forest walk to a waterfall in the afternoon.

stops.name: White-water rafting
stops.note: Grades I–IV depending on the stretch; operators drive you upstream and you raft back towards town. Not possible in July–August.

stops.name: Neer Garh waterfall walk
stops.note: A popular, well-marked trail to tiered pools above Tapovan.

days.travel: Rafting operators include transfers; the waterfall trailhead is a short taxi or auto ride from Tapovan.
days.meals: Light breakfast before rafting; lunch back in Tapovan.
days.logistics: Book only with licensed operators; life jackets and helmets are mandatory. Carry a change of clothes.

days.title: Day 5 — Sunrise at Kunjapuri and departure
days.summary: A pre-dawn drive to a hilltop Shakti Peeth for Himalayan views at sunrise, then onward travel.

stops.note: About 27.5 km up a winding hill road; book the taxi the night before.

stops.name: Kunjapuri Devi Temple
stops.note: At 1,676 m; climb the steps from the road for views of the snow peaks on clear mornings.

stops.name: Back to Rishikesh, then depart

days.meals: Tea at the temple stalls; breakfast back in Rishikesh.
days.logistics: Carry a warm layer — the hilltop is cold before dawn, especially October–March.

budget.assumptions: Per adult, sourced entry fees only. Hotels, rafting, taxis and yoga classes vary widely and are not estimated.

Book a day ahead with a licensed operator; confirm the stretch, grade and transfers.
Arrange a 4:45–5 am pick-up the evening before.
Book well ahead for the International Yoga Festival (first week of March) and long weekends.

alternatives: Travelling in July–August? Rafting is suspended — replace Day 4 with a Neelkanth Mahadev Temple trip (28 km into the forest).
Not a morning person? Do the Kunjapuri sunset instead and leave on Day 5 afternoon.
Families with young children can skip rafting and take a Rajaji National Park safari from Haridwar instead.
Want more yoga? Replace Day 4 with a full-day ashram programme.
tips: Rishikesh is vegetarian-only and alcohol-free; respect it.
Dress modestly at ghats and ashrams.
Keep to the forest path and the opening hours at the Beatles Ashram — it is inside a tiger reserve.
The Ganga is cold and fast; bathe only at ghats with chains and steps.

prep.title: Weather
prep.body: Summers in Haridwar are hot; December–January nights are cold. Monsoon (July–August) brings heavy rain, landslides on hill roads and no rafting.

prep.title: Crowds
prep.body: Kanwar Yatra (Shravan) and Kumbh years bring huge crowds and traffic restrictions; check dates before booking.

faqs.q: Haridwar or Rishikesh — where should I stay?
faqs.a: One night in Haridwar for the Har ki Pauri aarti, then Rishikesh for the rest: it is quieter, greener and has the yoga schools and rafting.
September to June. It is suspended in July and August during the monsoon.

faqs.q: How much is the Beatles Ashram ticket?
faqs.a: About ₹200 for Indian visitors; foreign visitors pay more, with listed fees ranging from ₹600 to ₹1,200. It is open 10 am–4 pm.
